Screen checkConfirm in Vanderbilt's Oracle or UKG during a recorded demo: the Workforce Structures > Positions path; the Term/Flex field name and rules; the part-time hours threshold; VTS (Vanderbilt Temporary Services) naming; that a regular HCM (not a super-user) sees Our Workforce and this quick action.

1 · Intro

When to use it.

Every hire starts with a position. The requisition is built from it, and the new hire's assignment inherits from it, so a mistake here follows the person all the way through.

First decide whether you need a new position or an update to an existing one. Then have the position description and, for a staff position, the pre-search memo from Compensation.

Use this whenYou need a position to recruit and hire into, and you need to decide whether to create a new one or update one you have.

2 · Walk through

Step by step.

Follow along in Oracle HCM. Check off each step as you go.

New position or update?
SituationDo this
A new role in your business unitCreate a new position
More seats with the same job and locationUse one pooled position (headcount more than 1)
A seat in a different locationCreate a separate position
The business unit changesCreate a new position; positions can't move between business units
A vacant position built for another worker typeCreate a new position; don't repurpose it
An inactive position you want to use againReactivate it only if it meets current guidelines; otherwise create a new one
The same role's name, job code, category, work unit, or location changesUpdate the existing position

Before you submit

The same four checks on every pay-impacting transaction. Draft: the owner for this area confirms anything marked To confirm.

Attach

  • Pre-search memo from Compensation Required
  • Approved position description Attach

Check

Read every field back against the source document: person, effective date, position, hours, pay, and costing.

  • Effective date is today, not the start date.
  • The six-digit job code and assignment category match the memo.
  • Location is where the person would sit on site.
  • Standard working hours stay at 40. Working hours hold the actual hours.

Cutoff

No payroll cutoff applies to a position. It must be approved and active before it can be posted or used, so date it today.

Who does what

  • Who starts it: You.
  • Who approves: To confirm: the approval chain for this transaction.
  • What happens next: Once approved, the position can go on a requisition. The hire inherits from it.

Watch-outs

  • An inactive position that no longer meets current guidelines, such as one with an old job code, can block updates and approval. Bring it up to date or create a new one.
  • Don't repurpose an unused position that was built for a different worker type (for example, a student position for staff). Create a new one.
  • The requisition copies the position when it is submitted. Fix the position before you create the requisition.
  • Fields that get positions sent back: Standard working hours (always 40), Job (the code from the memo), Assignment category (never Professional salaried non-exempt), Manager (leave blank), Attachments (the memo for a staff position).
  • Open item: confirm the job code, assignment category, and pre-search memo rules for positions that are not staff positions (students, postdocs, interns, affiliates, contractors).

Official documentation

Vendor documentation describes the standard process. Vanderbilt's setup, codes, and rules in this course take priority.

  • Oracle: Jobs and Positions (Using Global Human Resources) (opens in a new tab)

HCM Academy quick guide · Position Management

Create a position

Use when: You need a position to recruit and hire into, and you need to decide whether to create a new one or update one you have. · System: Oracle HCM

  1. Decide: a new position or an update?
    • Positions can't move between business units.
    • Fix the position before any requisition; the requisition copies it when submitted.
  2. Open Positions.
  3. Click Add (or Create).
  4. Effective date: today, not the start date.
  5. Status: Active. Action reason: New Position.
  6. Business unit, name, and code.
  7. Work unit: the department.
  8. Job: enter the job code from the pre-search memo.
    • Staff and faculty jobs mapped to the job architecture use six-digit codes.
    • Not every worker type has been mapped yet; positions for students, postdocs, interns, affiliates, and contractors may use other codes.
  9. Location: where the person would sit on site.
  10. Assignment category: the one on the memo.
  11. Hours: keep Standard working hours at 40; set Working hours to the actual hours.
  12. Headcount and type.
  13. Overlap allowed: Yes. Then set Term or Flex if it applies.
    • Temporary: six months or less.
    • Term: a fixed role longer than six months, up to a year.
    • Flex: needed only part of the year, such as summer help who return each year. Usually non-exempt; set as temporary with 20 working hours so benefits don't kick in.
  14. Attach the documents, add comments, and click Submit.
New position or update?
SituationDo this

The business unit changesCreate a new position; positions can't move between business units
A vacant position built for another worker typeCreate a new position; don't repurpose it
An inactive position you want to use againReactivate it only if it meets current guidelines; otherwise create a new one
The same role's name, job code, category, work unit, or location changesUpdate the existing position

Before you submit

  • Attach: Pre-search memo from Compensation (required). Approved position description (attach).
  • Check: Effective date is today, not the start date. The six-digit job code and assignment category match the memo. Location is where the person would sit on site. Standard working hours stay at 40. Working hours hold the actual hours.
  • Cutoff: No payroll cutoff. Date it today so it can be used.

Watch-outs

  • An inactive position that no longer meets current guidelines, such as one with an old job code, can block updates and approval. Bring it up to date or create a new one.
  • Don't repurpose an unused position that was built for a different worker type (for example, a student position for staff). Create a new one.
  • The requisition copies the position when it is submitted. Fix the position before you create the requisition.
  • Fields that get positions sent back: Standard working hours (always 40), Job (the code from the memo), Assignment category (never Professional salaried non-exempt), Manager (leave blank), Attachments (the memo for a staff position).
  • Open item: confirm the job code, assignment category, and pre-search memo rules for positions that are not staff positions (students, postdocs, interns, affiliates, contractors).

HCM Academy detailed job aid · Position Management

Creating a position, step by step

Step by step with screenshots. Screens from the HCM Academy training simulation of Oracle HCM. Names are fictional; check labels against Vanderbilt's Oracle.

  1. 01Decide: a new position or an update?

    Use the table below. A new role, or a seat in a different location or business unit, needs a new position. The same role changing, such as its name, job code, work unit, or location, is an update to the existing position (see Update a position).

  2. 02Open Positions.

    Sign in to Oracle Cloud with your VUnetID. On the Home page, go to Our Workforce, scroll to Workforce Structures, and click Positions. Click Search with the status filter set to Active to see every active position in your business unit; the Incumbents column shows who sits in each one.

  3. 03Click Add (or Create).

    A new position opens at the When and Why section.

  4. 04Effective date: today, not the start date.

    The position must be approved and active before it can be posted. If someone starts Oct 1, create the position effective today; dating it Oct 1 means it can't be used until Oct 1.

  5. 05Status: Active. Action reason: New Position.

    New positions always use these two values.

  6. 06Business unit, name, and code.

    Pick your business unit. Name is what you call the position (for example, Accounting Manager). Code identifies it; note it so you can find the position later.

  7. 07Work unit: the department.

    Where Oracle says department, it means work unit.

  8. 08Job: enter the job code from the pre-search memo.

    Search by code, not by name; the code returns the exact job (for example, Accountant Support SS2). The job name becomes the employee's business title and ties the position to Vanderbilt's job architecture, including pay ranges. Leave Manager blank: managers change, and the manager belongs on the assignment.

  9. 09Location: where the person would sit on site.

    Location feeds the requisition and the hire. It decides whether the posting must show a pay range (pay transparency states such as New York and California) and which pay range Compensation recommends. Don't assume Nashville. If the role is remote, the location is overridden on the assignment at hire.

  10. 10Assignment category: the one on the memo.

    For staff positions, use the category on the pre-search memo. Most used: Professional exempt, Staff non-exempt, and VTS (Vanderbilt Temporary Services). Never Professional salaried non-exempt: it's built into Oracle but not used at Vanderbilt, and the position will be sent back.

  11. 11Hours: keep Standard working hours at 40; set Working hours to the actual hours.

    FTE is calculated from standard working hours of 40. Typing 20 into Standard working hours makes the FTE 1 by mistake. For a 20-hour position: Standard 40, Working 20, FTE 0.5. This is the most common position error.

  12. 12Headcount and type.

    Headcount 1 is Single incumbent. More than 1 is Pool, and the FTE multiplies (3 full-time seats = FTE 3). Vanderbilt doesn't use None or Shared. Seats in different locations need separate single-incumbent positions.

  13. 13Overlap allowed: Yes. Then set Term or Flex if it applies.

    Overlap lets you recruit and hire into the position while the current incumbent is still on payroll.

  14. 14Attach the documents, add comments, and click Submit.

    For a staff position, central HR approves only with the pre-search memo attached (not needed for VTS). The position description helps your business unit approver. Attachments stay on the position, so you keep its history. Approval goes to your business unit approver (often the CFO), then to the central HR approval group.
